key_insight: The paper reconstructs molten-pool surface flow from high-speed video by combining optical flow with physics-informed neural networks that enforce fluid-mechanics constraints.
engineering_relevance: This enables noninvasive flow diagnostics for wire-arc DED, helping relate process conditions to bead geometry, defects, and microstructure.
method: Homography-correct oblique high-speed video and extract dense optical flow as raw velocity observations.
Train a PINN to satisfy data fidelity, incompressible Navier–Stokes momentum, no-penetration boundaries, and an arc-forcing prior.
Extend to a phase-conditioned time-dependent PINN for cyclic flow during periodic droplet impact.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation on high-speed imaging from a GTAW-based wire-arc DED process under two regimes: quasi-steady convection and periodic droplet impact.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of video calibration and optical-flow estimates, which may be sensitive to glare, occlusion, and strong thermal distortion.
paper_title: Reconstruction of Molten Pool Flow Fields from High-Speed Video Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
